chunks.text: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki wants rival AI labs to agree on limits for their most powerful models. In an essay published November 22, he proposes common limits based on perplexity and other measurements. Perplexity scores how well a model guesses the next piece of text. OpenAI published its own scores for the first time, falling from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to under 0.8 for its newest models. Labs would stay below the limits until they can understand and monitor model behavior. CEO Sam Altman backed the idea. Reports name no limit value, no start date, and no body to run it. For Gulf governments building AI capacity, watch whether shared limits become a standard they're expected to follow.
